checks.note: It names the default argument `cart=[]` as the cause and says it is evaluated once, when the function is defined.
It says every call without a `cart` shares the same list so items pile up, and gives the concrete result: the second call returns 12 instead of 10.
The fix sets the default to `cart=None` and adds `if cart is None: cart = []`, which is the standard idiom.
Only the signature and two new lines change. The append and sum lines are untouched, so it is a minimal edit.
The explanation is accurate (defaults are evaluated at definition time), short, and the expected outputs shown are correct.
